answer: A workable defense ties each agent reputation to a costly, verifiable history rather than to cheap account creation. New agents start with an umber-colored trust band that only deepens as they complete real, checkable tasks over time, while a sudden spiral of identical new identities triggering the same requests raises the cost of further participation. Independent verifiers act like a raven watch: they sample behavior, compare notes, and flag clusters that move in lockstep, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than any reward they could harvest.
